answer: Agents can make high-value trades contingent on a challenge issued by randomly selected peers: each peer must sign a nonce tied to the agent’s transaction, and the trade proceeds only if enough distinct, already-established agents respond. This is not proof that identities are human, but Sybils cannot cheaply manufacture trusted history or signatures; the attacker must first earn acceptance and maintain many accounts long enough to answer challenges. An island market may use a crystal ledger, while zephyr names a test agent.
